title: Slatewise QPS Regulator and Graceful Fallback Playbook for Embeddings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: High-variance tenant traffic (bursty spikes + long-tail p99) causes embedding workers to exhibit amplified latency and cross-tenant interference. Existing autoscalers react too slowly for short bursts and naive backpressure leads to broad error spikes. Goal: Implement a slatewise QPS regulator that applies tenant-scoped pacing windows, headroom-aware admission, and a graceful fallback strategy (degraded quality + local approximate embeddings) so customer-facing APIs keep stable latency and predictable cost during surges. Scope: 1) Admission control library (tenant-scoped rate windows + burst tokens). 2) Slatewise prioritization: group short-lived batch windows by tenant predicted QPS to optimize packing. 3) Graceful fallback paths: local lightweight approximate-embed (quantized model) + cached nearest-neighbor candidate rerank. 4) Autoscaler hooks to factor short-window percentiles (1s/10s) and cost budgets into fast-path scaling decisions. Out of scope: Full tenant SLA billing changes (billing team follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end internal load test: under a synthetic 10x spike from 1000 tenants, p95 embedding latency remains below 120ms and p99 below 400ms for 90% of tenants
Tenant-level QPS regulator applied with per-tenant burst allowance and observed reduction in cross-tenant tail latency (>=30% p99 improvement vs baseline)
Graceful fallback triggers for overloaded tenants and returns consistent response schema (fast_approx: true + fallback_reason), with documented quality delta measured on production-like evals
Autoscaler exposes short-window metrics (1s, 10s percentiles) and scales up within target reaction time (<=45s) for sustained load above configured headroom
Unit + integration tests for admission control, slate grouping, and fallback logic with >=90% coverage for the new modules
Runbook updated and on-call notified; chaos test executed without client-visible 5xx rate increase >1%
design_decisions: Use a token-bucket per-tenant with two buckets: steady-state (long window) and burst (short window) to allow controlled bursts without starving others
Slatewise grouping will use a lightweight tenant fingerprint and short-time histogram to route similar short batches into existing warm pools to increase packing efficiency
Fallback path will use a quantized 8-bit distilled embedding model co-located on CPU for immediate response; degrade quality but keep latency SLOs
Autoscaler decision layer will add a fast-path that consumes 1s/10s QPS percentiles and cost_headroom signals; the existing stable autoscaler remains the authoritative long-term scaler
Backpressure signals are binary and tiered: soft-defer (retry with progressive backoff), hard-drop (if over configured cost budget) with clear error codes for caller SDK handling
engineering_tasks: ENG-210988: lib/ingress: implement tenant token-bucket admission control and metrics hooks
ENG-210989: runtime: implement slatewise batcher and packing heuristics
ENG-210990: models: ship quantized local approx-embed model and packaging for CPU fallback
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fallback model quality regression could break downstream reranking. Mitigation: run A/B on representative evals and require quality delta < 4% on top-10 recall before enabling for a tenant

Risk: Token-bucket misconfiguration could starve bursty but latency-sensitive tenants. Mitigation: expose per-tenant override flags and default conservative burst allowances; require PM approval for higher bursts
Risk: Increased cost due to faster scaling. Mitigation: cost_headroom metric and hard budget threshold to allow hard-drop when necessary; provide telemetry for customer-reported cost spikes
Risk: Complexity increases SRE burden. Mitigation: limited rollout (canary 5% tenants), detailed dashboards, and an automated rollback flag in console
monitoring_and_observability: New metrics: tenant_token_bucket_fill, tenant_burst_consumed, slate_pack_rate, fallback_trigger_count, fallback_quality_delta
Dashboards: per-tenant QPS heatmap, global p95/p99 before/after regulator, autoscaler reaction histogram
Alerts: p99 latency increase >50% vs baseline for >5min (sev-2), fallback_trigger_count spike >500/min (investigate)
Logging: structured event for each fallback with tenant_id, reason, model_version, and candidate_cache_keys
